subject: Datawaypoints & transit certification — request for subprocessor attestations
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@datacrest.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, procurement@datacrest.com
Cc: DataCrest Security Team <security@datacrest.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:12:00Z
Subject: Quick Q on where requests actually run (data transit / subprocessors)

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We are reviewing Redwood for PII processing in our customer-support workflow. Two quick asks from our security team before we move to legal: can you provide a short, plain-language mapping of where a single inference request travels (regions/hops) and a list of subprocessors involved per hop?

Specifically:
- If a request originates from our app in EU (eu-west-1), can you confirm which Redwood components and third-party services may receive or touch that payload, and in which regions?
- Any cross-border egress to the US or APAC? If yes, what subprocessors and controls apply?
- We also need a concise attestation or pointer to an internal doc that shows data erasure/retention behavior per processing hop.

If you have a one-pager or a minimal diagram we could attach to our procurement file that’d be ideal.

Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Security, DataCrest
oliver.grant@datacrest.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@datacrest.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T17:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where requests actually run (data transit / subprocessors)

Hi Oliver —

Appreciate the clear asks. Looping in Marissa (Security & Compliance) and Karthik (Solutions) to provide the mapping and the attestation artifacts. I'll assemble a short summary and a diagram.

High-level preview (short):
- Inbound from eu-west-1: initial routing happens in our EU ingress layer (self-hosted or cloud-hosted in EU).
- Model execution: if you choose EU-only execution we route to EU compute pools (GCP europe-west3 / AWS eu-west-1) — otherwise hosted defaults may include US pools for capacity fallback.
- KV/prefix caching and analytics: transient telemetry and caching may be stored in region-local caches; longer-term telemetry is aggregated in US analytics clusters (with pseudonymization).
- Subprocessors: primary infra providers (AWS/GCP), CDN for edge ingress, and tracing/monitoring partners. We’ll send a per-hop roster with region tags.

Marissa/Karthik — can you confirm the exact subprocessors and attach the one-pager + the attestation language we can share with procurement? We have a short "datawaypoints" diagram I can attach.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@datacrest.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where requests actually run (data transit / subprocessors)

Hi Oliver / Sofia —

Attaching a concise pack (see links below and attached CSV):
- redwood_subprocessor_roster.csv (attached) — lists subprocessors, region/endpoint, and contractual role (processor/subprocessor).
- datawaypoints-diagram.png (attached) — minimal hop diagram (ingress → routing → execution → cache/kv → telemetry) labeled by region.
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (attached) — high level controls map.

Short answers to your bullets:
1) EU-originating request (eu-west-1) — if customer pins "EU-only execution" we guarantee routing to EU compute pools (GCP eu-west3, AWS eu-west-1). In that configuration no model payload leaves EU compute pools for execution; transient cache keys used for performance are also pinned to EU caches.
2) Cross-border egress — if customer selects default hosted tier and capacity is constrained in EU we may route execution to compatible model variants in US or APAC. In those fallback cases the subprocessors below would be involved:
   - AWS (us-east-1) or GCP (us-central) for execution
   - Edge CDN partner (FastEdge) for ingress acceleration
   - Monitoring/tracing partner (TraceWise) for telemetry collection (telemetry pseudonymized)
   All cross-border routes are covered by SSDs in our DPA, standard contractual clauses where applicable, and documented encryption-in-transit + at-rest.
3) Erasure / retention per hop — model inputs are ephemeral. By default request payloads are kept transiently for inference (milliseconds → minutes); KV caches have configurable TTLs. We provide APIs to purge customer-specific caches and a guaranteed asynchronous deletion timeline for logs/aggregates in our analytics (default 30 days, configurable on enterprise plans). For EU-only pin customers, logs and telemetry retention follows your configured retention window and is stored in-region.

If you need a signed attestation for procurement, we can produce a short letter that enumerates subprocessors and confirms execution locality and erasure commitments for a specified configuration (e.g., EU-only, EU-first fallback, Global-default). That attestation can be signed by our Head of Compliance.

Links / attachments:
- Drive (pack): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/DataCrest-transit-pack
- HubSpot record: HS-DC-87

Let us know which configuration you plan to commit to (EU-only vs Global-default) and we’ll prepare the signed attestation.

—
Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@datacrest.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@datacrest.com
Date: 2026-11-23T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Datawaypoints & transit certification — request for subprocessor attestations

Marissa / Sofia —

This is exactly what we needed, thank you. A couple of follow-ups before procurement signs off: 
- Could you confirm whether the CDN partner (FastEdge) ever persists payloads, or is it strictly a pass-through?
- For the SOC2 summary: can you confirm which controls cover cross-border routing decisions (i.e., who can flip a region fallback policy and what auditing exists)? We may ask for a short excerpt we can attach to our security review.

If you can provide the signed attestation for an "EU-only execution + EU cache" configuration, that will unblock contracting on our side. Procurement wants explicit subprocessors listed and a signature.

Oliver
